key_insight: MedRLM reframes clinical AI as a recursive, multimodal reasoning system that can repeatedly inspect, retrieve, verify, and synthesize long patient histories, images, sensor data, and guidelines.
clinical_relevance: The approach is designed to support more auditable decision-making, earlier screening triggers, and better referral planning across community-to-tertiary care settings.
method: Uses specialized agents for clinical text, EHR, imaging, sensor signals, guideline retrieval, uncertainty auditing, and referral planning.
Builds a Clinical Evidence Graph Memory to link patient findings with evidence, biomarkers, and referral criteria.
Triggers deeper recursive reasoning when abnormal sensor patterns or low-confidence outputs are detected.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a real-data evaluation plan using public and credentialed datasets spanning EHR, radiology, ECG, ICU time series, and referral-proxy outcomes.
watch_item: Because the framework depends on multiple data sources and recursive agent coordination, implementation may be complex and requires careful validation to avoid propagation of errors or overconfident recommendations.
paper_title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
